investigation.title: Remote Agent Eval Failure: Kubernetes kata.peerpods.io/vm Resource Exhaustion Blocking Pod Scheduling
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because the Kubernetes scheduler could not place the agent pod: only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource and both are at capacity, while the remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity or selector. No VM was ever assigned, so the eval runner never received orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, or remoteState, causing a total contract gap against the expected-output contract defined in infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents swarm has exhausted the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource on the 2 nodes that carry it. Every new remote-agent pod is Unschedulable because 0/6 nodes are available: 2 report Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm and 4 do not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Preemption cannot help because no lower-priority victims exist on those nodes. Because no pod ever reaches a running state, the eval runner's createAgent call (run-status-probes.mjs line 1885) never returns a VM identity, leaving all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) absent. This is an eval-detected infrastructure capacity failure localized to the kata.peerpods.io/vm node pool; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

investigation.title: Remote Agents: All Three Checks Failing Due to Kubernetes kata.peerpods.io/vm Resource Exhaustion
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api between 12:52 and 12:57 UTC on 2026-07-22 with identical Kubernetes scheduling errors: the cluster's 6 nodes could not schedule the eval's remote agent pod because only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource and both were at capacity, while the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the pod never scheduled, the agent was never created, and the eval runner could not collect any evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state), causing the remote-agent-state contract to fail with zero evidence returned.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent eval environment has exhausted its available kata.peerpods.io/vm resource slots. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-runtime) confirms that the two nodes capable of hosting peer-pod VMs were both fully allocated when each of the three eval pods was submitted. Preemption was also unavailable ("No preemption victims found"). As a result, the createAgent call in run-status-probes.mjs (line 1905) never returned a live agent, the state-polling logic never executed, and the required evidence fields orgId, agentId, readyState, and state were never written, violating the contract defined in check-expectations.json line 264. This is an eval-infrastructure failure scoped to the Kubernetes VM resource pool; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource pool exhausted on both capable nodes at eval time: the scheduler explicitly reports 'Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' on 2/6 nodes and no preemption victims were available. All three sibling checks hit the same condition across a ~5-minute window, indicating sustained exhaustion rather than a transient spike.

Secondary — node affinity/selector mismatch on 4/6 nodes: the eval pod requires a node label or taint that only 2 nodes satisfy. If those 2 nodes were not exhausted but the selector was misconfigured, the same error would appear. However, the explicit 'Insufficient' qualifier on the 2 matching nodes makes resource exhaustion the more likely primary cause.

Tertiary — a concurrent workload (non-eval) consumed the remaining kata.peerpods.io/vm slots on both capable nodes just before the eval window, leaving no capacity for the probe pods. This is consistent with all three checks failing sequentially rather than simultaneously.

Lower confidence — a cluster scaling or node-readiness event reduced the number of kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes below the normal baseline, making the pool smaller than expected. No node-event evidence is present in the packet to confirm or deny this.

investigations.title: Image Generation Stream Eval Failure: OpenAI Billing Hard Limit Reached on /api/generate/image/stream
investigations.summary: The image-generation-stream eval failed because the OpenAI API returned a hard billing limit error (billing_hard_limit_reached) when the runner called /api/generate/image/stream, causing the stream to terminate with a generation_error frame instead of a generation_completed frame and no image URL artifact. Both required contract assertions — frameTypes containing "generation_completed" and imageUrlPresent equaling true — were violated as a direct consequence of this upstream billing rejection.
investigations.rootCause: The OpenAI account or API key used by the eval runner has hit its configured billing hard limit. When the runner at infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs (lines 1981–1986) called /api/generate/image/stream with model gpt-image-2, the OpenAI API immediately rejected the request with error code billing_hard_limit_reached and type billing_limit_user_error. The backend propagated this as a generation_error SSE frame (GENERATION_FAILED), preventing the stream from ever emitting generation_completed or an image URL. This is an external dependency (billing/quota) failure, not a code defect in the eval runner or contract definitions.
proof: failed-check.message: generation_error frame data contains OpenAI error {"message":"Billing hard limit has been reached.","type":"billing_limit_user_error","code":"billing_hard_limit_reached"}
failed-check.evidence: frameTypes observed are [generation_start, generation_start, generation_progress, generation_error, message] — generation_completed is absent
failed-check.evidence: imageUrlPresent is false, confirming no artifact URL was produced
failed-check.timing: latencyMs=810 — the stream terminated in under 1 second, consistent with an immediate API rejection rather than a generation timeout

expected-output.contract: assertions require frameTypes to contain generation_completed and imageUrlPresent to equal true (infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json lines 339–344), both of which are unmet

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1978-1986: runner calls /api/generate/image/stream with model gpt-image-2 using the configured API key — the billing error originates at this external call boundary
possibleCauses: Primary: The OpenAI billing hard limit for the account or API key used by the eval runner has been reached, causing all image generation requests to be rejected immediately by the OpenAI API.
Secondary: The API key configured for the eval runner belongs to an account with a low or exhausted spending cap that was not replenished before this run.

Tertiary: The AURA_STATUS_IMAGE_MODEL environment variable resolves to gpt-image-2 (confirmed in source-context run-status-probes.mjs line 1986), which may have higher per-request cost, accelerating billing limit exhaustion.
Lower probability: A misconfigured or rotated API key is being used that maps to a different billing account already at its limit.

investigations.title: model-matrix eval failure: aura-gpt-5-5 returned 502 due to upstream Anthropic 429 rate-limit error
investigations.summary: The model-matrix check failed because 1 of 2 configured models (aura-gpt-5-5) returned a 502 bad-gateway error during its runtime test call. The 502 body explicitly identifies an upstream Anthropic 429 Too Many Requests rate-limit error as the cause, meaning AURA's backend was unable to reach the model provider at the time of the eval run. The other model (aura-claude-sonnet-4-6) passed cleanly, confirming the failure is isolated to the aura-gpt-5-5 model slot and not a systemic eval infrastructure problem.
investigations.rootCause: The AURA runtime harness received an HTTP 502 bad-gateway response when invoking POST /api/agents/[REDACTED]/runtime/test for model aura-gpt-5-5. The 502 payload contains an embedded Anthropic API 429 rate_limit_error with the message "AURA is temporarily unable to reach the model provider. This is an issue on our side, not with your account or credits. Please try again shortly." This indicates that at the moment the eval ran (2026-07-22T12:48:50Z–12:50:13Z), AURA's server-side proxy to the Anthropic API was being rate-limited or throttled for the aura-gpt-5-5 model route, causing the runtime test to fail and the allPassed and failedModelCount assertions to be violated. This is an eval-time transient provider-side condition, not a confirmed user-facing production outage; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

expected-output.contract: assertions require allPassed=true and failedModelCount=0; both are violated exclusively because of the aura-gpt-5-5 result.

failed-check.timing: latencyMs=83801, well within the warningLatencyMs=180000 and outageLatencyMs=360000 thresholds defined in source.infra/evals/status/features.json:249, ruling out a latency-based failure.
possibleCauses: Primary: Transient Anthropic API rate-limit (429) on the aura-gpt-5-5 model route at the time of the eval run, surfaced as a 502 from AURA's runtime harness. The error message explicitly states this is a server-side issue, not an account or credential problem.

Secondary: Sustained or recurring rate-limit exhaustion on the AURA backend's Anthropic quota for the aura-gpt-5-5 model specifically, which would cause repeated eval failures rather than a one-time transient.

Tertiary: A misconfiguration or routing issue specific to the aura-gpt-5-5 model identifier in AURA's runtime that causes it to be routed through a quota-constrained Anthropic API path, while aura-claude-sonnet-4-6 uses a separate path that is not affected.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Eval Failure: Kubernetes kata.peerpods.io/vm Resource Exhaustion Blocking Pod Scheduling
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because the Kubernetes scheduler could not place the agent pod: only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource and both are at capacity, while the remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity or selector. No VM was ever assigned, so the eval runner never received orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, or remoteState, causing a total contract gap against the expected-output contract defined in infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents swarm has exhausted the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource on the 2 nodes that carry it. Every new remote-agent pod is Unschedulable because 0/6 nodes are available: 2 report Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm and 4 do not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Preemption cannot help because no lower-priority victims exist on those nodes. Because no pod ever reaches a running state, the eval runner's createAgent call (run-status-probes.mjs line 1885) never returns a VM identity, leaving all four required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) absent. This is an eval-detected infrastructure capacity failure localized to the kata.peerpods.io/vm node pool; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

[Possible] A prior eval run or leaked agent pod from a previous withCleanup cycle is holding a kata.peerpods.io/vm slot and was not released before this run started, reducing available capacity.

[Possible] The node affinity/selector on the remote-agent pod spec restricts scheduling to a subset of nodes that does not include any node with remaining kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity, making the effective pool smaller than the total 2 eligible nodes.
[Lower likelihood] A node carrying kata.peerpods.io/vm became NotReady or was cordoned between runs, reducing the eligible pool from a previously larger count to exactly 2.

investigations.title: Remote Agents: All Three Checks Failing Due to Kubernetes kata.peerpods.io/vm Resource Exhaustion
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api between 12:52 and 12:57 UTC on 2026-07-22 with identical Kubernetes scheduling errors: the cluster's 6 nodes could not schedule the eval's remote agent pod because only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource and both were at capacity, while the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the pod never scheduled, the agent was never created, and the eval runner could not collect any evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state), causing the remote-agent-state contract to fail with zero evidence returned.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent eval environment has exhausted its available kata.peerpods.io/vm resource slots. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-runtime) confirms that the two nodes capable of hosting peer-pod VMs were both fully allocated when each of the three eval pods was submitted. Preemption was also unavailable ("No preemption victims found"). As a result, the createAgent call in run-status-probes.mjs (line 1905) never returned a live agent, the state-polling logic never executed, and the required evidence fields orgId, agentId, readyState, and state were never written, violating the contract defined in check-expectations.json line 264. This is an eval-infrastructure failure scoped to the Kubernetes VM resource pool; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource pool exhausted on both capable nodes at eval time: the scheduler explicitly reports 'Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm' on 2/6 nodes and no preemption victims were available. All three sibling checks hit the same condition across a ~5-minute window, indicating sustained exhaustion rather than a transient spike.

Secondary — node affinity/selector mismatch on 4/6 nodes: the eval pod requires a node label or taint that only 2 nodes satisfy. If those 2 nodes were not exhausted but the selector was misconfigured, the same error would appear. However, the explicit 'Insufficient' qualifier on the 2 matching nodes makes resource exhaustion the more likely primary cause.

Tertiary — a concurrent workload (non-eval) consumed the remaining kata.peerpods.io/vm slots on both capable nodes just before the eval window, leaving no capacity for the probe pods. This is consistent with all three checks failing sequentially rather than simultaneously.

Lower confidence — a cluster scaling or node-readiness event reduced the number of kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes below the normal baseline, making the pool smaller than expected. No node-event evidence is present in the packet to confirm or deny this.

investigations.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted to the Kubernetes cluster was rejected as Unschedulable: the two nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining four nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. No remote agent VM was ever provisioned, so the eval runner never received any response evidence and all five required contract fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) are missing.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes: 2 nodes with the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource had insufficient remaining capacity, and 4 nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector rules. Preemption was also unavailable on both resource-constrained nodes. Because the pod never became Running, the agent was never created, no runtime response was produced, and the eval evidence object remained empty — causing a total contract gap for all five required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message). This is an eval-observed infrastructure scheduling failure localized to the remote-agents feature in production-api; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: Most likely — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhausted on the two eligible nodes: all available peer-pod VM slots are consumed by existing workloads, leaving no capacity for new eval pods. This is directly stated in the scheduler message (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-state).

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the pod spec targets nodes with the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource via affinity/selector rules, but 4 of 6 nodes do not match those rules, reducing the schedulable pool to only 2 nodes. If those rules have become overly restrictive (e.g., after a node label change), capacity would appear lower than actual.

Tertiary — cluster under-provisioning: the production-api cluster has only 2 nodes capable of hosting kata peer-pod VMs. If concurrent eval runs or production workloads have consumed all VM slots simultaneously, new pods will queue and time out.

Lower confidence — transient scheduling spike: a burst of concurrent remote-agent pod requests (e.g., from multiple eval runs or production traffic) temporarily exhausted the VM resource pool, which may self-recover once existing pods are released.
